brand_names: Paula's Choice Skin Perfecting 1% BHA Lotion
Some By Mi AHA BHA PHA 30 Days Miracle Toner
what_its_for: This product helps treat and remove milia, which are tiny white or yellowish bumps that appear just under the skin's surface. It works by gently exfoliating the top layers of skin, loosening dead skin cells, and unclogging pores so that trapped keratin (a skin protein) can be released. It may also help with blackheads, whiteheads, and overall uneven skin texture.
how_to_take: This is a topical (applied to skin) product — do NOT swallow it. Apply it only to clean, dry skin on the affected area. Use a cotton pad or clean fingertips to gently dab or sweep a small amount of the essence onto the areas with milia. Let it absorb fully into your skin before applying other skincare products. Do not rub aggressively — gentle application is all you need. Always apply sunscreen during the day when using this product, because salicylic acid can make your skin more sensitive to the sun.
dosing: Use once daily, preferably in the evening (at night), especially when you are first starting out. Once your skin gets used to the product (usually after 2 to 4 weeks), you may use it up to twice daily — once in the morning and once at night — if your skin tolerates it well. Start with a small amount (a few drops or one cotton pad's worth) applied only to affected areas. Do not apply more than directed, as using too much can irritate your skin.
missed_dose: This is a skincare product, not a prescription medication, so there is no strict dosing schedule. If you forget to apply it one day, simply continue with your normal routine the next day. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed application. Consistency over time is more important than any single application — just try to use it regularly as part of your daily skincare routine.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from direct sunlight, heat, and humidity. Do not store in the bathroom if it gets very steamy. Keep the cap or lid tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze. Check the expiration date on the bottle and do not use after it has expired. If the product changes color, smell, or texture, discard it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using this product near your eyes, inside your nose, inside your mouth, or on broken, cut, or severely irritated skin. Do not use it on open wounds. Avoid combining it with other strong exfoliating products (such as retinol, AHAs like glycolic or lactic acid, or benzoyl peroxide) at the same time without guidance from a dermatologist, as this can cause excessive dryness, peeling, and irritation. Avoid prolonged sun exposure without sunscreen while using this product — always wear SPF 30 or higher sunscreen during the day. Do not use waxing, laser treatments, or other harsh skin procedures on treated areas without talking to your doctor or dermatologist first. Avoid applying to large areas of the body beyond what is affected.
when_to_call_doctor: Stop using the product and contact your doctor or dermatologist if you experience: severe redness, burning, or stinging that does not go away after a few minutes of application; blistering, swelling, or peeling skin; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat; skin that becomes very dry, cracked, or raw; any unusual skin reaction or worsening of your skin condition. Also call your doctor if you accidentally swallow any of the product or if it gets into your eyes and rinsing with water does not relieve irritation.
when_it_works: Salicylic acid works gradually. You may begin to notice your skin looking smoother and milia starting to shrink or disappear within 4 to 8 weeks of consistent daily use. Some people see improvement sooner, while others may need up to 3 months. Be patient and use the product regularly. If you do not see any improvement after 3 months of consistent use, talk to your dermatologist, as some milia may require professional removal.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals: Consult your doctor or pharmacist before using salicylic acid products during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. While 1% salicylic acid applied to small skin areas is generally considered low risk, it is always best to get medical advice first. Children under 12 years old: This product should generally not be used on young children without a doctor's recommendation. Elderly individuals: Older adults may have more sensitive or thinner skin, so start with less frequent use (every other day) and monitor for irritation. People with sensitive skin or skin conditions such as eczema, rosacea, or psoriasis: Use with extra caution and consult your dermatologist before starting. Those with aspirin (salicylate) allergies: Do not use this product, as salicylic acid belongs to the same family of chemicals and may trigger a reaction.
